ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT rules are in Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 to R.561-63 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). The beneficial-owner definition is principally in Article L.561-2-2 and Article R.561-1. Beneficial-owner information for legal entities is governed principally by Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and Articles R.561-55 to R.561-63 of the Monetary and Financial Code, together with Articles L.123-6 and R.123-123 et seq. of the Commercial Code and the French National Business Register rules. The register is maintained through the Guichet unique operated by the National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding and periodically thereafter, screen all founders, shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, UBOs, intermediaries, distributors, banks and material counterparties against United Nations Security Council sanctions, European Union sanctions implemented in France, French national restrictions, OFAC SDN and relevant OFAC lists, UK sanctions where commercially relevant, and reputable PEP and adverse-media databases. Apply enhanced due diligence for PEPs, relatives and close associates under Articles L.561-10 and L.561-10-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code. Verify identity, source of wealth, source of funds, control rights, sanctions ownership and control, and beneficial ownership through the entire chain. Do not treat OFAC measures as automatically applicable to a purely non-US transaction, but assess US nexus, USD clearing, US persons, US-origin technology and secondary-sanctions exposure. File a suspicious transaction report with TRACFIN where legally required; do not disclose the report to the subject.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: French Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr/, operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); resulting registration data is recorded in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE) and, for commercial entities, the competent commercial registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the French incorporation documents and must comply with French public-order, trademark, company-law and consumer-protection rules. French does not generally require a SAS corporate name to be written in French or in a local script, but foreign words, abbreviations and transliterations must be clear and must not create confusion with an existing company, protected designation, public authority or registered trademark. The name should be checked against the RNE, INPI trademark database, EUIPO records, domain names and relevant trade-name databases. A French-language certified translation may be required for foreign supporting documents, not ordinarily for the corporate name itself.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting a public authority, ministry, regulator, court, diplomatic body or governmental status without authorization

Protected professional or regulated-activity designations, including terms implying banking, insurance, investment services, payment services, healthcare-professional status or pharmaceutical status without the required authorization
Terms implying a licensed medical-device, pharmaceutical, clinical, laboratory or therapeutic activity beyond the company's actual authorization and conformity status
Names contrary to public order, morality, consumer protection, or prohibitions against discrimination, fraud or misleading commercial presentation
Existing or confusingly similar company names, business names, trademarks, domain names or protected geographical indications

The terms Société Anonyme, SA, Société Européenne, SE, Société Coopérative, bank, credit institution, insurance or equivalent protected designations where use could mislead or breach applicable sector legislation
Terms reserved or regulated under the Commercial Code, Monetary and Financial Code, Public Health Code, Intellectual Property Code or sector-specific legislation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation procedure with a universal 30-day reservation period for a SAS. Conduct availability checks before signing the articles, reserve matching domains and, where commercially important, file a trademark application with INPI or EUIPO. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects or suspends the filing, obtain the written reason, correct the articles or supporting documents, and resubmit through the Guichet unique within the stated cure period. If the decision is attributable to the competent registry, use the available administrative or judicial remedy indicated in the decision, including referral to the president of the competent commercial court where applicable for a registry refusal or omission. Trademark refusals or objections must be challenged before INPI within the prescribed opposition or appeal deadline, or before the competent court where judicial review is available. A name rejection does not itself create a statutory extension right.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a registered office in France under Articles L.123-11 and R.123-167 et seq. of the Commercial Code. A domiciliation company or compliant virtual office may be used if the provider is authorized and the domiciliation contract satisfies French requirements. A director's private residence may be used subject to statutory conditions and applicable lease, condominium and planning restrictions. For Class III medical-device manufacturing, virtual-office use is insufficient as operational substance: the company requires an appropriate manufacturing, quality-system, storage, traceability, vigilance and regulatory location. A separate production site must comply with Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices, applicable French Public Health Code requirements, CE-marking and conformity-assessment obligations, and any ANSM or notified-body requirements. A registered virtual office should therefore be limited to corporate correspondence and must not be represented as the manufacturing or regulatory site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official French statistical probability is published for unannounced inspections. The risk is materially higher than ordinary low-risk commercial incorporation because coronary drug-eluting stents are generally Class III medical devices and the business has high-risk AML, product-safety, customs and regulated-manufacturing characteristics. Planning assessment: low for a newly incorporated dormant holding or administrative entity, medium for a trading entity, and high for an operating manufacturer, importer or distributor. Potential inspections or audits may involve ANSM, the competent health authorities, customs, labor authorities, tax authorities, notified bodies, accreditation bodies and the commercial registry. A numerical probability should not be represented as an official rate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French environmental standards for industrial emissions, wastewater discharge, and waste management including VOC and laser-related fumes

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural inspections by SDIS (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours), plus workplace safety clearances under the French Labor Code

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate formalities and legal/tax identifier registration submitted through the Guichet Unique operated under the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) must file an incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique. Upon successful registration the company automatically obtains a SIREN/SIRET number, a French tax identification number, and, when necessary, an intra-EU VAT identification number. The VAT/TIN allocation is electronic, typically completed within two to four weeks after submission of the static constitutive documents and identification of directors and beneficial owners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SAS is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Available statutory election/adjustment mechanisms: (i) election to be taxed as a persona with limited passthrough for qualifying small SAS structures and certain dedicated holding/professional property companies under Article 239 quinquies of the CGI; (ii) election to integrate into a French IS tax consolidation group (intégration fiscale) where a French-resident entity holds at least 95% of the SAS shares; (iii) election for the reduced corporate rate applicable to 'young innovative enterprises' (JEI status) if the SAS carries on eligible R&D-intensive medical-technology activities; (iv) hybrid-mismatch election/disclosure obligations under Article 61 CGI implementing EU BEPS Action 2 and requiring submissions on structured arrangements leading to outcomes inconsistent with French or foreign tax characterisation; no US-style check-the-box election is available in France.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax — taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €85,000 annual taxable turnover for sale of goods (including processed goods and medical-device manufacturing output); €37,500 annual taxable turnover for other services; threshold applies under Article 293 B of the French CGI and is assessed on a calendar-year/ongoing-activity basis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has enacted a phased e-invoicing and e-reporting reform: issuance of structured electronic invoices (Factur-X or PEPPOL BIS 3.0) via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified private platform; mandatory from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-cap entities, and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro enterprises; B2B invoicing flows and B2C e-reporting will be transmitted in near-real time to the DGFiP. For export transactions to non-EU territories, clearance is effected through the customs declaration (DAU) in the EU Customs Decision System and supporting transport evidence; no continuous electronic VAT stamping of each export transaction is imposed for zero-rating purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union are zero-rated if the physical movement of the goods to a non-EU territory is demonstrated and evidenced. For class III coronary drug-eluting stents, zero-rating requires actual shipment from the EU, sale to a non-EU customer, and proof that the goods left the customs territory of the European Union within the regulatory time window. Intra-EU supplies of the stents may also benefit from a 0% rate if the acquirer is identified for VAT in another EU member state, the goods are dispatched to another EU member state, and an intra-community acquisition report is documented; failure to meet the documentary burden converts the supply into a domestic taxable transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/customs declaration in the Single Administrative Document system – EX-A or EX-AU)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (connaissement / lettre de transport aérien)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank attestation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If an export zero-rating claim is unsupported, false, or corrected after inspection, the DGFiP recharacterises the transaction as a domestic supply and assesses TVA at the applicable rate (20% for medical devices unless separately classified). Civil penalties include 40% of the tax due for deliberate neglect or fraud (manquement délibéré), 80% for abusive manoeuvres (abus de droit) and an additional 0.2% monthly late-payment interest (intérêts de retard). Criminal consequences may include fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment for tax evasion directors, together with joint several liability of corporate managers. The statute of limitation is extended to six years for undisclosed BFEE-linked offshore arrangements.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties_no: The 180-day repatriation benchmark is treated as the administrative safe-harbour expectation for export proceeds in a tax audit context; delays beyond 180 days require a documented banking/trade justification to avoid exchange-control and transfer-pricing scrutiny.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.legislative_references: Code générale des impôts (CGI) Articles 8, 209, 256–262, 292, 293 B, 1731–1732; Code monétaire et financier Article L561; VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; French Finance Law e-invoicing articles (Loi de finances 2023); LOI governing permanent-establishment concepts absent for SAS absence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains a regime of full capital account convertibility as a founding member of the Eurozone. Capital transactions including equity injections, dividend remittances, and interest payments are freely convertible without quantitative restrictions. Residents must file declarations with the Banque de France for transactions exceeding €100,000 to support statistical reporting. Profit remittance is subject only to standard corporate tax clearance and beneficial ownership verification; no additional FX surrender obligations apply to intra-EU flows. Current account transactions benefit from automatic convertibility with mandatory bank reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: French exporters must repatriate all foreign exchange proceeds within twelve months of shipment date. Banks require original commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents, and proof of export delivery. No mandatory surrender ratio exists; proceeds must be credited in EUR to the exporter's designated account. Non-compliance may result in regulatory referral to the Banque de France and administrative penalties under the Monetary and Financial Code. All companies must retain supporting documentation for at least ten years.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions such as N26 or Revolut offer limited cross-border corporate treasury services for French SAS entities. Legal constraints include absence of full banking license, strict AML obligations, and regulatory prohibition on handling Class III medical device payments due to elevated risk classification. Offshore digital EMIs cannot support full export clearing or hedging functions and require additional French banking partner integration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must attend physical KYC interviews at the bank branch. Remote video verification is permitted only for existing clients or lower-risk operational accounts; new corporate accounts involving medical device manufacturing require in-person presence to satisfy enhanced due diligence and face-to-face identification requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification for Class III medical device manufacturing and potential dual-use technology exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle including SAS registration certificate, manufacturing license, export contracts, end-user certificates, beneficial ownership declarations, source-of-funds evidence, and proof of compliance with French export control regulations and international sanctions screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQU'. Verification requires shareholder resolutions, equity contribution agreements, tax residency certificates, and beneficial ownership declarations. Banks perform source-of-funds analysis and may request additional documentation for transactions exceeding €100,000. All movements must comply with Banque de France reporting thresholds and French exchange control regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements cleared through SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600. Medical device exports typically utilize LCs for security. Disbursements require compliant shipping documents, invoices, proof of delivery, and end-user certificates. Purpose codes such as 'TRADE' or specific export codes must be stated. All outbound payments undergo full AML screening and FX control compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts for EUR/USD and other major pairs to hedge transaction exposure
Currency swaps for multi-period liquidity management
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for hedging non-EUR exposures
Options contracts for asymmetric risk protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory auditor's report (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) via the Single Electronic Filing Portal (guichet des formalités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the ordinary shareholders' meeting approving the annual accounts; the meeting must be held within six months of fiscal year-end, so the filing is due no later than seven months after the accounting year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing penalty of up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 7,500 for a repeated offence), plus possible court-ordered injunction to file under legal penalty; after 30 days from formal notice, administrative dissolution and judicial removal from the RCS may be initiated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory when an SAS exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at fiscal year-end: total balance sheet exceeding EUR 4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8 million, or average workforce exceeding 50. Other statutory triggers include listed status, public-interest activity, or banking/insurance scope.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory financial statements under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général); consolidated accounts of listed and other public-interest entities under IFRS as adopted by the European Union; optional IFRS for consolidated accounts of non-listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France requires no standalone annual UBO filing; the beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) must be filed with the RCS and kept accurate at all times. Any share transfer that changes the direct or ultimate beneficial ownership chain must be declared within 30 days. At the annual shareholders’ meeting, the executive president must verify that the UBO declaration on file is still accurate and confirm it in the minutes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholder decisions and deliberations (registre des délibérations d’associés)
Securities-movement register recording all share transfers, issuances and conversions (registre des mouvements de titres)
Attendance sheets and powers of attorney for shareholder meetings (feuilles de présence et pouvoirs)

stage_6.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year in DD/MM/YYYY format.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a SAS owned by non-residents, use the statutory French calendar year (closing 31 December) unless the general meeting has elected a different interval, disclosed on the first return.
